assessments.reasoning: Section 5.5 maps x to the first vector component, permits replication when selecting values, and excludes a repeated component when the selection is used as an l-value. Its assignment example directly exercises a repeated first component.

challenge.method: Independently map the selector letters onto component positions for a vector with components 3, 5, 7, 11. Compare reading xx, writing xx, and selecting the distinct components xw of the same writable base.
challenge.results: The read selects positions zero and zero, giving (3, 3). The repeated position violates the separate l-value rule even with a correctly typed right operand. The xw sample contains distinct positions and is not a counterexample to the prohibition on repetitions.

limitations: This concerns a valid writable vec4 and an otherwise type-compatible ordinary assignment. It does not generalize to scalar swizzles, naming-set mixtures, or all possible writable expressions.
